A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GradSAE work. All ten pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SQuAD perturbation and local-steering experiments in Table 1, plus latent-overlap, layer-sensitivity and cross-SAE results in Tables 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Table 1 and Appendix D, Tables 3–5.

M1.justification: Gradient-times-activation scoring, token averaging, positive-influence selection and latent interventions remain unchanged. Removing the lossless-reconstruction wording does not change the decoder equation or procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use SQuAD validation data for question-answering perturbation and local steering between questions sharing a context. No dataset, domain or task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same activation-only Baseline is compared with GradSAE in Tables 1, 4 and 5. No evaluated comparator is added, removed or revised.

E3.justification: Both retain the same correctly answered sample selection, greedy decoding, EM/F1 metrics, text normalization and K settings. Gemma and LLaMA model configurations and tested layers also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D retains the same latent-overlap analysis, layer-choice sensitivity tests and cross-SAE generalization experiment. Their analytical questions and supporting evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix C specifies random seed 42 in both versions. Neither version reports additional repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results and reported findings in Tables 1 and 3–5 are unchanged. For example, GradSAE retains 80.45% EM for K=1 perturbation and 10.21% F1 for K=10 local steering in Table 1.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), the influence definitions and Appendix A's first-order Taylor derivation remain unchanged. The reconstruction wording edit does not alter the formal definitions or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same hypotheses about unequal latent influence and effective steering, and the same claimed contribution of gradient-based latent identification.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 removes the assertion that SAE reconstruction is lossless, modestly qualifying the mechanism description. Result interpretations and the stated restriction to instruction-tuned question answering remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the anonymous 4open.science code address with the GitHub repository Tizzzzy/sae_gradient. Implementation and hardware disclosures remain unchanged; the PDFs establish a changed access instruction, not improved repository contents or availability.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged. Shu et al.'s survey reference changes from an arXiv preprint to Findings of EMNLP 2025, which updates publication metadata for the same work.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short funding Acknowledgments section, edits the reconstruction wording and updates bibliographic metadata. The main narrative, section ordering and appendix organization otherwise remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 removes printed page numbers and locally reflows the abstract and references around the updated link and acknowledgments. Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–5 retain their content, structure, captions and placement.

improvement.justification: Removing the blanket lossless-reconstruction assertion in Section 2.1 modestly improves precision and consistency with the existing reconstruction-fidelity discussion. Added funding disclosure improves transparency. These are limited gains; the method, empirical support, proof and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
